relations.rationale: If Yara is in the same class as Milo and Milo is in the same class as Zeno, then Yara should be in the same class as Zeno, making the combination consistent but 14 alone supports transitive class membership.
Yara being in the same class as Milo does not directly determine whether Yara is or isn't in the same class as Zeno without more information.
Yara's class relationship with Milo has no bearing on when Zeno joined the choir.
Kai's height relative to Hugo has no bearing on Hugo helping stack chairs.

If Milo is in the same class as Zeno, and Yara is not in the same class as Zeno, this implies Yara is not in the same class as Milo, but 16 alone doesn't confirm 19; however it makes 19 more plausible if combined with other facts, though alone it doesn't directly relate to Yara.
Milo being in the same class as Zeno doesn't inform how long Zeno has been in the choir.
Milo's class membership with Zeno has no bearing on Milo's singing tenure.
The pianist running through opening bars twice doesn't directly cause or indicate sopranos' pitch struggles on the third measure.
The pianist practicing bars twice has no bearing on whether the next rehearsal is scheduled.
Sopranos struggling with pitch doesn't relate to Milo's singing history.
Yara's class relationship with Zeno has no bearing on Hugo stacking chairs.
Zeno joining the choir a year ago is a separate fact from Milo's long-standing membership, neither confirming nor denying each other.
Zeno's recent joining of the choir has no bearing on Kai offering to lock up the hall.
Hugo helping stack chairs and Kai offering to lock up are both plausible end-of-rehearsal actions but neither implies the other.
Hugo stacking chairs as rehearsal ends doesn't inform whether the next rehearsal is scheduled.
Kai offering to lock up after everyone leaves doesn't relate to whether the next rehearsal is already scheduled.
